Types already allow both forms. Done.

## What was wrong

In `parseCacheControlHeader` (`lib/util/cache.js`), a qualified `private`/`no-cache` directive with an empty argument produced a bogus field-name list:

- `private=""` → `{ private: [''] }` — an array containing an empty header name. Because `canCacheResponse` only bails out on `private === true` (`lib/handler/cache-handler.js:432`), a *shared* cache would happily store a response marked `private=""`.
- The same happened for `private=" "`, `private=", "`, and a lone `private="`.

While fixing that I hit an adjacent crash: mixing the unqualified and qualified forms in one header (`private, private=x` or `no-cache, no-cache="a"`) threw `output[key].concat is not a function`, since the code concatenated onto the boolean `true` set by the unqualified branch.

## The fix

`lib/util/cache.js:171` adds `addQualifiedFieldNames`, now used by both the quoted and unquoted qualified branches. It trims and drops empty field names; if nothing is left, the directive is recorded as the unqualified `true` (the conservative reading — `private=""` qualifies no fields, so it applies to the whole response). It also leaves an already-unqualified `true` alone instead of calling `.concat` on it.

Behavior now:

| header | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `private=""` | `{private:['']}` | `{private:true}` |
| `private=` | `{private:true}` | `{private:true}` |
| `no-cache=""` | `{'no-cache':['']}` | `{'no-cache':true}` |
| `private, private=x` | throws | `{private:true}` |
| `private="a, b"` | `{private:['a','b']}` | unchanged |

## Verification

Added two tests to `test/cache-interceptor/utils.js` covering the empty-argument forms and the qualified/unqualified mix. `node --test test/cache-interceptor/*.js` → 68 pass, 0 fail; `node --test test/interceptors/cache.js` also passes. I could not run `npx eslint` — the command needed approval — so the style of the new code is matched by eye against the surrounding file. Nothing committed.
